brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
A broken black tea from Huaxi district in Guiyang, Guizhou, made by a tea farm there and known for its high, fresh aroma.

Treat it as you would any black tea: water just off the boil, a few minutes in the pot, and a seller who can say where it was grown.
history: The farm says it has exported its black tea since 1970 to Britain, West Germany, the Netherlands, West Asia, Australia and the United States. It was rated a quality provincial product in 1979 and 1980, and its No. 2 broken grade won a Ministry of Commerce award in 1985 and 1988.
processing: Typical of black tea: withered, rolled, fully oxidised and dried.
harvest_season: Picked through the growing season, as with most black teas.
taste_profile: Fresh and mellow, with a high, brisk aroma.
vintage_note: Black teas are normally sold by harvest year and are best within a couple of years.
